newsitem.title: UK: Caspian sells FilmFair, Paddington Bear.
newsitem.headline: Caspian sells FilmFair, Paddington Bear.

text.p: Caspian Group Plc, the media company which owns Leeds United Football Club, is to sell its FilmFair Ltd children's television programming catalogue plus certain rights to Paddington Bear to Canadian television company Cinar Films Inc for 10.54 million stg.

Under the deal, Cinar is buying over 100 hours of children's programmes, the assets of The Shoe People Ltd and Juniper Jungle Ltd, the Paddington Bear rights held by Caspian and the lease of Caspian's production facility.
Cinar is paying 5.5 million stg in cash, 3.79 million in subordinate voting shares and repaying 1.25 million in loans.

Caspian said it had considered keeping the children's programming catalogue but was unable to find suitable acquisitions to make it a sufficiently commercial proposition. It bought the catalogue in 1991 for 1.75 million stg.

The company said it to spend the proceeds on developing its sports and media interests, which include Sport in Question for Carlton Television, Multi Media Television Productions Ltd and Racing World Ltd.
Caspian also reported a loss after interest and tax for the six months to June 30 1996 of 80,000 stg, against a 541,000 loss last time.
The group, which bought Leeds United in August, said it plans to become a sports, leisure and media group through vertical integration.

It said current trading was well ahead of comparable figures for last year. Football turnover had been enhanced by new kit and club sponsorship deals, increased TV income and sales through new retail outlets.
